question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=-\operatorname{csch}⁡g,\,g={x}^{2}
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=2x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g\cdot 2x \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡{x}^{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
